source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"To identify only bacterial infections because viral respiratory illnesses are not relevant to visitor screening","B":"To replace hand hygiene, source control, ventilation, and other infection-prevention measures in the facility","C":"To reduce introduction and spread of respiratory pathogens as one part of layered infection prevention","D":"To permanently exclude all visitors because symptom screening cannot be adjusted to community transmission"}}
source_row.rationale: CDC advises healthcare facilities to use layered respiratory infection-prevention practices. Visitors with respiratory symptoms should be advised about source control and may be encouraged to defer non-urgent visits until recovered.
source_row.source_detail: Visitor and respiratory hygiene recommendations; current healthcare guidance accessed 2026-08-14.

source_row.stem: Why may a hospital screen visitors for respiratory symptoms during periods of increased community respiratory illness?
